a3481.speech: Reported that Nigeria recorded $15.2 billion in net foreign exchange inflows in the first quarter of 2025, with total FX inflows rising to $28.92 billion while outflows stood at $13.72 billion ; reported that gross external reserves declined in the first quarter of 2025 due to seasonal factors and foreign debt interest payments, even though it anticipates a "steady uptick" throughout the year.

a3481.speaker: Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN)
a3481.speech: Reported a 63.7% increase in international money transfer operator inflows during the first nine months of 2024, rising to $3.82 billion from $2.33 billion in the corresponding period of 2023.

a3481.speaker: World Bank
a3481.speech: According to the World Bank, Nigeria received $19.5 billion in diaspora remittances in 2023, representing 35% of sub-Saharan Africa's total remittance inflows, though this marked a 2.9% year-on-year decline from previous levels.

a3481.speaker: African Union
a3481.speech: Has expressed concerns about the discriminatory nature of expanded travel restrictions.

a3512.speaker: John Jinapor, Minister for Energy and Green Transition of Ghana
a3512.speech: Has disclosed that 40 of the over 1300 missing ECG containers have been retrieved after they were traced to an Indian man ; said a foreign national, an Indian man, has been arrested after national security operatives picked intelligence that he was in possession of 40 of the missing containers, which he had kept at a warehouse in Kpone ; revealed that upon interrogation, the Indian claimed that the 40 containers were sold to him last year ; noted that law enforcement agencies are still investigating the case and assured that all the missing containers would be retrieved and that the persons responsible would face the law ; “The briefing I got this morning and let me commend the National Security Operatives and the law enforcement agencies, the information I got is that already they've traced about 40 of them to a particular terminal warehouse in Kpone which belonged to an Indian man and they have confiscated all the 40 containers and moved them to a secured location. The man indicates that those containers were sold to him last year and so that's a matter of investigation that law enforcement agencies would ensure that the law takes its course. There are also reports of some other areas that they are picking intelligence, they will trace and retrieve all of them and fish out the perpetrators before the court of competent jurisdiction.”

a3512.speaker: John Jinapor, Minister for Energy and Green Transition of Ghana
a3512.speech: Cautioned, “Let me just say that when we start prosecuting these people, let no one say that this is witch-hunting. These are properties of the state, and we will use every legitimate means to ensure that we retrieve them.”

a3512.speaker: John Abdulai Jinapor, Minister of Energy and Green Transition (on receiving the investigation findings)
a3512.speech: Described the situation as alarming and assured that a full-scale investigation involving the Attorney-General and the Police would be conducted to track down the missing containers or recover their monetary value.

a3512.speaker: Investigative report on the ECG
a3512.speech: Revealed that more than 1,300 containers intended for clearance at the Tema Port were unaccounted for.

a3512.speaker: Prof. Innocent Senyo Acquah, chairman of the investigative committee
a3512.speech: According to him, ECG initially claimed to have 2,491 uncleared containers filled with cables and other essential equipment; however, an independent audit at the port found only 1,134 containers, leaving 1,347 missing.

a3512.speaker: Indian national arrested over the containers (unnamed)
a3512.speech: Claimed that the 40 containers were sold to him last year.

a3588.speaker: Israeli forces
a3588.speech: stated that the crowd waiting for the food distribution constituted "a threat."

a3588.speaker: Sources heard by the AFP news agency (anonymous)
a3588.speech: denied responsibility for the high number of dead, indicating that dozens of people were injured in "pushing and trampling" after they had surrounded trucks carrying humanitarian aid and begun looting them.

a3588.speaker: Health Ministry of the Hamas movement, which controls the Gaza Strip
a3588.speech: declared 104 dead, holding Tel Aviv responsible.

a3588.speaker: Hamas
a3588.speech: "The attack was premeditated and intentional, in the context of the genocide and the ethnic cleansing of the people of the Gaza Strip. The occupation army knew that these victims had come to this area to obtain food and aid, but killed them in cold blood."

a3588.speaker: Gaza Health Ministry
a3588.speech: said on Wednesday that six children had died of malnutrition and dehydration in the north of the territory over the past two days.

a3588.speaker: United Nations
a3588.speech: According to the United Nations, about 2,300 trucks entered Gaza in February, 50% fewer than in January.

a3588.speaker: Government of Gaza (statement issued today)
a3588.speech: "We hold the American administration, the international community, the occupation and the international organisations responsible for the murder of civilians who are dying of hunger at the hands of the occupation."

a3588.speaker: Hamas
a3588.speech: accused "the occupation" of trying to "starve" the inhabitants of Gaza and says that more than 700,000 people are suffering from hunger in the north of the enclave.

a3588.speaker: Gaza authorities
a3588.speech: have reported the deaths of more than 30,000 Palestinians, in addition to more than 400 in the West Bank and East Jerusalem, due to the actions of the security forces and Israeli attacks.

a3670.speaker: Joseph Utsev, Nigerian Minister of Water Resources and Sanitation
a3670.speech: Said the Federal Government has taken proactive measures to prevent the further spread of cholera in the country ; Speaking at the 5th Lagos State International Water Conference, said the ministry has reactivated its laboratories across the six geopolitical zones, embarked on massive sensitization campaigns, and emphasized the importance of personal hygiene, proper water treatment, and cooking of food and vegetables.

a3670.speaker: Joseph Utsev, Nigerian Minister of Water Resources and Sanitation
a3670.speech: Urged state governors, traditional and religious leaders to scale up campaigns against open defecation and build more decent toilets to achieve an open defecation-free target by next year.

a3670.speaker: Babajide Sanwo-Olu, Governor of Lagos State
a3670.speech: Acknowledged a huge gap in achieving access to clean and safe water for citizens, calling for more support from the Federal Government and development partners.

a3839.speaker: Saada Abdillahi (USAID representative), Abdi Dirir (Director General of Education, MENFOP) and Fozia Ali (Director of the MFF)
a3839.speech: In their opening remarks, underlined the importance of collaboration among the various stakeholders to ensure the success of the project and the continued improvement of access to preschool education in Djibouti.

a3839.speaker: Director of a school supported by the Play To Learn project
a3839.speech: Shared his experience in a video shown at the workshop, underlining the improvements made to infrastructure and teaching methods, allowing children to develop in a more inclusive and stimulating setting.

a3839.speaker: Mother of a child attending a school supported by the project
a3839.speech: Gave testimony expressing her deep gratitude for the benefits of the project, explaining how access to quality preschool education had transformed the life of her child, who has made significant progress, both academically and socially.

a3876.speaker: Pope Leo XIV (Robert Francis Prevost)
a3876.speech: Stressed the symbolic importance of the day: “It is a gift from God that my first Sunday as Pope in Rome coincides with that of the Good Shepherd” ; expressed gratitude for the presence and joy of the faithful: “Thank you for bringing warmth to the feast of Christ” ; quoted Saint Gregory the Great, saying that “people respond to the love of those who love them,” and expressed his joy at praying together with the pilgrims present.

a3876.speaker: Pope Leo XIV (Robert Francis Prevost)
a3876.speech: Confessed to feeling “profound pain” in the face of the ongoing conflicts both in the Middle East and in Europe: “I am deeply saddened by what is happening in the Gaza Strip. Let there be an immediate ceasefire. Humanitarian aid must reach the exhausted civilian population, and all hostages must be released.”

a3876.speaker: Pope Leo XIV (Robert Francis Prevost)
a3876.speech: Referring to the war in Ukraine, expressed solidarity with the Ukrainian people, saying he carries their sufferings in his heart, and concluded by calling for “an authentic, just and lasting peace” for the country.

a3959.speaker: Pascal Irénée Koupaki, Minister of State of Benin
a3959.speech: Announced at his press briefing on Wednesday 12 October that Benin had obtained from the Inter-State High Council of the Benin Electricity Community (CEB) a waiver for the purchase and import of additional electrical energy on the community's interconnected grid, an opportunity seized by the Ministry of Energy "to identify a private energy producer that can immediately offer an additional capacity of 60 MW to Benin" ; revealed that the Council of Ministers authorised the minister in charge of Energy "to conclude, with the assistance of a specialised consulting firm, at the best price, a contract for the purchase of an additional 60 MW of power from the company Paras Energy," and that the Minister of the Economy and Finance was instructed "to contribute to raising the necessary financing as quickly as possible."

a3959.speaker: Pascal Irénée Koupaki, Minister of State of Benin
a3959.speech: Said that "in order to clean up relations between the Beninese Electricity Company (SBEE) and the CEB, the ministers of the Economy and Finance and of Energy, Water and Mines have been instructed to initiate the process of clearing SBEE's arrears towards the CEB"; stressed that the financial arrangement for this clearance will be handled by the Minister of the Economy and Finance, to the tune of 12 billion CFA francs, and announced the imminent examination by the government of the debts and claims between the State and SBEE.

a4018.speaker: Libyan government (declaration lodged with the ICC)
a4018.speech: Declared the country’s acceptance of the ICC’s jurisdiction with respect to alleged crimes in its territory from 2011 to the end of 2027.

a4018.speaker: International Criminal Court (29th report / statement to the UN Security Council)
a4018.speech: Noted that it had seen ” an unprecedented six months of dynamism in our work in the situation in Libya” ; “There is what can be described as a black box of suffering on the coast of the Mediterranean that nobody has wanted to open. A black box that contains the cries, the ongoing pain, as we speak, of some of the most vulnerable people in both the West and the East of the country”, on the subject of Libyan detention facilities and potential crimes committed there.

a4018.speaker: Ambassador Christina Markus Lassen, Permanent Representative of Denmark
a4018.speech: Commended the ICC prosecutor’s office for their work in Libya by highlighting the unsealed arrest warrants for alleged crimes and efforts to ensure that the voices of victims and survivors are heard.

a4043.speaker: Myrian Vieira, Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Cabo Verde (SENEC)
a4043.speech: Says Cabo Verde has known how to take consistent and coherent positions in the international arena; in this interview with Expresso das Ilhas she analyses the international political situation and also some points that have marked the national political agenda, such as the financing of the embassies or the opening of a diplomatic representation in Morocco.

a4043.speaker: Ambassador of Cabo Verde to the United States
a4043.speech: Says our country does not have the resources to secure the defence of its territory and its sea on its own, and that therefore the government did well to sign the SOFA agreement with the United States, and that the derogation of jurisdiction under cover of the Vienna Convention does not violate any constitutional norm.

a4143.speaker: Chinese government (official position statement)
a4143.speech: Published on Saturday its position opposing the abuse of tariffs by the United States, stating that the United States has recently imposed tariffs, under various pretexts, on all its trading partners, including China, seriously compromising the legitimate rights and interests of nations, seriously violating World Trade Organization rules, seriously harming the rules-based multilateral trading system and seriously disrupting the stability of the world economic order. The Chinese government strongly condemns this measure and firmly opposes it ; the measures taken by the United States violate basic economic principles and market norms, disregard the balanced results achieved in multilateral trade negotiations and ignore the fact that the United States has long benefited substantially from international trade. The use of tariffs as a tool of extreme pressure for selfish ends is a typical example of unilateralism, protectionism and economic bullying ; under the cover of “reciprocity” and “fairness,” the United States engages in zero-sum games and essentially seeks “America First” and “American exceptionalism” ; the United States exploits tariffs to overturn the existing international economic and trade order, prioritizing American interests over the global common good and sacrificing the legitimate interests of countries around the world to serve its own hegemonic agenda ; “Such actions will inevitably meet broad opposition from the international community” ; “We do not create trouble, but we never back down from it,” stressing that pressure and threats are not the right ways to deal with China, and that China has taken and will continue to take resolute measures to safeguard its sovereignty, security and development interests ; the United States must stop using tariffs as a weapon to suppress China’s trade and economy, and stop undermining the legitimate development rights of the Chinese people ; China will open its doors further to the outside world, whatever the evolution of the international situation, continuing to open at a high level, regularly expanding its institutional opening in rules, regulations, management and standards ; “Openness and cooperation being the trend of history, the world will not and must not retreat into mutual isolation and division” ; “The international community has a shared responsibility to make economic globalization more open, more inclusive, more universally beneficial and more balanced” ; development is a universal right for all countries, not the exclusive privilege of a few, and international affairs must be discussed and handled collectively ; there are no winners in trade or tariff wars, and protectionism leads to a dead end; all countries must uphold extensive consultation, joint contribution and shared benefits, defend true multilateralism, work together to oppose all forms of unilateralism and protectionism, and defend the UN-centred international system and the WTO-centred multilateral trading system ; the great majority of countries that value fairness and justice will remain on the right side of history; the world must embrace fairness and not hegemony.

a4143.speaker: Embassy of the People's Republic of China in Mali
a4143.speech: Cited as the source of the text.

a4186.speaker: François Abiola, Vice-Prime Minister of Benin (representing the President of the Republic)
a4186.speech: Insisted at length on the government's support; he sees SIMA as a “highly musical and then cultural event” which, in his words, confirms that it is “like a travelling market of African music,” while also testifying to “the willingness of professionals in the music sector to accompany the public authorities in promoting the music industries on the African continent.”

a4186.speaker: François Abiola, Vice-Prime Minister of Benin
a4186.speech: Said SIMA is “an opportunity for the government to provide proof that the Beninese public authorities have remained attached to cultural entrepreneurship” and do “not intend to depart from the tradition of African public authorities' support and of enabling African artists to circulate.” He also sees in it a crucible for the promotion of tourism in Africa and in Benin.

a4186.speaker: Eric Gbèha, Vice-President of BEMA (Bureau export de la musique africaine), the organising body
a4186.speech: Indicated that the event must be situated “within a dynamic of complete revolution of the music sector in Africa so as to enthrone it at the scale of the global forums where professionals gather, reflect and accelerate the pace of international musical development…”, and recalled that the venture launched in Yaoundé in 2013, continued in Dakar in 2014, should be reinforced this year in Cotonou in the perspective of a “positive competition.”

a4189.speaker: Civil Protection of the Palestinian territory (Gaza)
a4189.speech: According to information from the Civil Protection of the Palestinian territory, at least 85 civilians died as victims of Israeli attacks this Tuesday in the Gaza Strip.

a4189.speaker: Ministry of Health of Gaza
a4189.speech: According to the Gaza Health Ministry, two bombardments in northern Gaza that hit a family home and a school converted into a shelter for displaced people resulted in the deaths of 22 people, more than half of them women and children. Other attacks in Deir al-Balah, in the centre of the Strip, and in the Nuseirat refugee camp caused 13 and 15 deaths respectively. In Khan Younis, two attacks killed 10 people.

a4189.speaker: Israeli army
a4189.speech: stated that the targets were Hamas command centres and that it had warned civilians in advance. Israel justified the attacks by claiming that Hamas operates in densely populated areas, which, according to Tel Aviv, contributes to civilian deaths.

a4189.speaker: Pope Leo XIV
a4189.speech: appealed this Wednesday for greater collaboration from the parties to allow access to humanitarian aid, with a view to easing the life of the population. The Pope was speaking in St Peter's Square at the Vatican, where he presided over his first General Audience.

a4523.speaker: Selibe Mochoboroane, Minister of Health of Lesotho (on the US withdrawal from the WHO)
a4523.speech: Announced that of the executive orders passed by US President Donald Trump, only two affect the health systems in the country ; "The first executive order that affects Lesotho is the departure of the US government from the World Health Organisation. America accounts for 18 percent of the contributions made by member countries which equates to around USD 500 million," ; indicated that this impacts on the country because it touches on WHO's budget in Lesotho: "Last year WHO injected M30 million toward the country's health sector, this means that WHO will not be able to inject the same amount this year. However, it does not imply that the organisation will fail to deliver services to its recipients," ; said that the WHO budget will be affected, but it does not mean it will not be able to render services to the health systems of its member countries.

a4523.speaker: Selibe Mochoboroane, Minister of Health of Lesotho (on the USAID freeze and the government response)
a4523.speech: Said the second order is the freezing of USAID, which helps the country with issues pertaining to HIV/Aids, TB and testing commodities, a move that has greatly affected the employment of 1 500 employees employed by partners working with the ministry ; "When the orders were executed, I informed the government as the ministry and rounded up all in party to come up with way to ensure that Basotho's livelihoods are not shaken," ; "There are 240 000 Basotho on Antiretroviral drugs. The government buys 73 percent of the drugs with the assistance of Global Fund securing 23 percent. Looking into matters Global Fund is not affected by the orders," ; on testing commodities, said they looked into the stock they have and how the supply chain will allow the lab to operate for the next three months: "The country has in stock enough commodities to last lab operations for about five to nine months subject to change if any disruptions occur," ; said the ministry convened with their partners to draw up salary costing of employees on government scale: "It will cost the government M27 million to assure employees from USAID funded programs are paid at government scale," ; was excited to have learned that the PEPFAR waiver has been accepted, indicating that the organisation is to continue with all projects relating to HIV/Aids testing, treating and lab operations.

a5194.speaker: Jacques du Toit, American embassy spokesperson (statement)
a5194.speech: Said in a statement Wednesday that US ambassador Lisa Johnson will participate in the send-off of a consignment of charcoal from Namibian supplier, Africa Burns Charcoal, to a US buyer ; “The shipment of 350 tons represents a landmark deal for the charcoal exporter. The deal was facilitated by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID)” ; said that after signing an agreement with the Namibia Charcoal Association (NCA), of which Africa Burns Charcoal is a member, USAID facilitated relationships with charcoal exporters and buyers for sustainable and long-term business.

a5395.speaker: Robert Dussey, Togolese Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5395.speech: Explicitly raised the possibility of Togo joining the AES, stressing that it would offer "access to the sea for member countries".

a5395.speaker: Ibrahim Traore, President of Burkina Faso
a5395.speech: At the swearing-in of Ghanaian President John Mahama in January 2025, as a special guest, confirmed the desire for closer ties with Accra.

a5395.speaker: King Mohammed VI of Morocco
a5395.speech: In November 2023, proposed access to the Atlantic Ocean for the AES countries.

a5395.speaker: Foreign ministers of Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso
a5395.speech: At a meeting in Rabat in 2025, welcomed this initiative [Morocco's Atlantic access offer], but no concrete timetable has yet been announced.

a5439.speaker: H.E. Muhammed B.S. Jallow, Vice President of the Republic of The Gambia
a5439.speech: Welcomed delegates on behalf of the President, H.E. Adama Barrow, and described the meeting as a “historic milestone” in consolidating the Court’s mandate ; noted that the new Arbitration Rules will enable the ECOWAS Court to provide a credible regional mechanism for resolving commercial disputes, thereby strengthening investor confidence and supporting the objectives of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

a5439.speaker: H.E. Alpha Sesay, Attorney General and Minister of Justice of Sierra Leone, Chair of the ECOWAS Ministers of Justice
a5439.speech: Described the court as “a beacon of justice and a symbol of our collective commitment to regional integration and the rule of law” ; “Our work here will have significant impact on the role that the Court continues to play in the sub-region and will strengthen access to justice for our citizens. Through this, we honour our duty to the protection of human rights, promotion of regional integration, and the resolution of disputes through arbitration.”

a5439.speaker: H.E. Dawda A. Jallow, Attorney General and Minister of Justice of The Gambia
a5439.speech: Delivering his keynote address, underlined the importance of equipping ECOWAS with arbitration tools comparable to international standards ; stressed that the Community Court of Justice has the potential to become a continental hub for arbitration and reaffirmed the need to empower it to address both human rights and economic disputes within the region.

a5439.speaker: Hon. Justice Ricardo Cláudio Monteiro Gonçalves, President of the Community Court of Justice
a5439.speech: Said that the Harmonised Protocol reflects “lessons learned over more than two decades of judicial practice” and ensures alignment with the Revised ECOWAS Treaty and decisions of the Authority of Heads of State and Government ; stressed that the Protocol will “reinforce the Court’s ability to discharge its mandate effectively,” while safeguarding the principles of justice, equity, and human rights that underpin the ECOWAS integration project ; added that the adoption of these instruments will shape the future of the Court and strengthen the credibility of the ECOWAS legal order.

a5439.speaker: Madam Miatta Lily French, ECOWAS Resident Representative to The Gambia
a5439.speech: Commended the President of the Court and his team for the initiative to ensure the work of the Court is made less cumbersome, and to enhance the effectiveness of the Court.

a5439.speaker: ECOWAS Ministers of Justice
a5439.speech: Reaffirmed their commitment to ensuring that the adoption of the Harmonised Protocol and Arbitration Rules strengthens the Community Court of Justice to deliver on its mandate and advance regional integration.

a5550.speaker: Fabian Lai, Acting CEO of the National Oil Company of Liberia (NOCAL)
a5550.speech: Delivered a comprehensive progress report on NOCAL's 23-year partnership with TGS NOPEC, saying the strategic partnership has resulted in the acquisition of an extensive multi-client 2D and 3D seismic survey programme covering over 15,000 square kilometers of Liberia's offshore basins, positioning Liberia as a promising player in the energy sector.

a5550.speaker: Fabian Lai, Acting CEO of NOCAL
a5550.speech: Emphasized the partnership's economic impact, stating that Liberia currently receives 80% of revenues from legacy 3D data sales.

a5550.speaker: Fabian Lai, Acting CEO of NOCAL
a5550.speech: Indicated that the partnership is not just about data and profits, but also about empowering the people and building a future where Liberians lead their energy sector.

a5550.speaker: Fabian Lai, Acting CEO of NOCAL
a5550.speech: Revealed annual contributions of US$200,000 for social and welfare programs, including the renovation of the ICU and expansion of the trauma unit at the John F. Kennedy Medical Center (US$15,000 total investment), medical equipment valued at US$60,000 and ICU beds costing US$142,955 ; highlighted the support for market women and the Group of 77 by providing US$40,000 towards initiatives that benefit women entrepreneurs and the disabled.

a5550.speaker: Fabian Lai, Acting CEO of NOCAL
a5550.speech: Shared his leadership's plans to attract additional investment with the anticipated executive allocation and conduct further geological and geophysical studies onshore, and plans for a feasibility study on constructing a shore base to support offshore exploration activities ; reaffirmed his team's unwavering commitment to leveraging the partnership with TGS NOPEC for the collective benefit of all Liberians and emphasized their determination to ensure that the energy sector transforms into a cornerstone of national development.

a5550.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, President of Liberia
a5550.speech: Lauded TGS NOPEC for its enduring partnership and highlighted its significant role in the country's frontier oil and gas industry and national development.

a5550.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, President of Liberia
a5550.speech: Underscoring the difficult circumstances faced by the country, particularly regarding the reduction in USAID aid, proffered the need for increased CSR contributions in order to solidify TGS NOPEC as a responsible partner ; further mandated a follow-up with TGS NOPEC on increasing its CSR contributions, while also exploring additional avenues for collaboration.

a5554.speaker: Florah Mpetsane, North East District chairperson
a5554.speech: Told the ongoing full council meeting in Masunga that a total of 28,213 cattle and 16,760 goats had been returned to the district and only 55 dairy cattle still remained to be purchased and distributed to affected farmers ; said government had decided to compensate all farmers before the end of February 2015.

a5554.speaker: Florah Mpetsane, North East District chairperson
a5554.speech: Said the new Botswana Animal Identification and Trackback System (BAITS) would be rolled out to districts by March throughout the country ; said that all necessary information on the new system would be availed by the Ministry of Agriculture.

a5777.speaker: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) (press statement sent to the newsroom)
a5777.speech: Approved yesterday financing of 500 million US dollars for the implementation of Compact II in Mozambique; according to the statement, the signing of the Financing Agreement between the Governments of Mozambique and the United States, through the MCC, is foreseen for September of this year in Washington DC; Compact II, approved in Washington, will focus on Zambézia province, covering three areas: Promotion of Investment in Commercial Agriculture; Connectivity and Rural Transport; and Climate Change and Coastal Development.

a5828.speaker: Nardos Bekele-Thomas, Resident Coordinator of the United Nations System in Benin
a5828.speech: "The needs are enormous because of the floods. We will continue to do the best we can to bring a rapid and effective response to the populations," she said on Monday.

a5828.speaker: Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a5828.speech: Estimates that of the 680,000 Beninese affected by the floods, about 200,000 people need shelter; more than 55,000 homes have been destroyed, 128,000 hectares of crops devastated and 81,000 head of livestock wiped out; in total 55 of the country’s 77 provinces have been affected.

a5828.speaker: Moumini Ouedraogo, WFP Director in Benin
a5828.speech: "At this stage, food is one of the priorities for the disaster-stricken populations," stressed Ouedraogo. "Several families have lost their harvests because of the devastating floods, and if we do not act quickly, the consequences risk being disastrous," he warned.

a5828.speaker: Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a5828.speech: Indicates that donors have also shown their support for the flood victims: the government of Japan sent emergency aid of blankets, tents, tarpaulins and mats; the mobile operator MTN donated 63,000 dollars to Caritas for food and 600 insecticide-treated mosquito nets; and Bank of Africa provided financial support of 25 million CFA francs to humanitarian activities.

a5828.speaker: Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) (latest estimates)
a5828.speech: According to the latest OCHA estimates, 1.8 million people are affected by the floods in West and Central Africa.

a5962.speaker: Julien Paluku, DRC foreign trade minister
a5962.speech: Defended the 12-month ban on importing beer, soft drinks, lime, earthenware and tiles from Zambia, citing his aim to lower import taxes, safeguard local businesses, boost their output, and combat the import fraud prevalent in DRC border posts.

a5962.speaker: Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo
a5962.speech: Said it was within its rights, enshrined in the 2015 trade pact with Zambia, to restrict the named products from entering its markets; said it would adhere to the trade agreement, which stipulated that restrictive measures could not go beyond four years; said it was acting to protect itself from being a dumping ground for goods that were likely “being subsidised or sold at such a low price as to cause injury to the local industry”; and said Zambia’s border closures were “not covered by the trade agreement”, initiating talks with Zambia as a result.

a5962.speaker: DRC-Zambia trade agreement of 6 August 2015 (document)
a5962.speech: Provides that each signatory has the right to “safeguard measures in respect of a product on conditions that it causes or threatens to cause serious injury to the domestic industry producing like or directly competitive products”, and that Zambia was meant to lodge a written complaint.

a5962.speaker: Zambia Association of Manufacturers (ZAM), statement issued by Ashu Sagar, ZAM president
a5962.speech: Said the move by the DRC presented big challenges to regional trade as well as Zambia’s manufacturing sector and economic stability: “The sudden cessation of imports will disrupt established supply chains, leading to potential revenue losses, the under-utilisation of production capacity, and the potential closure of operations that were heavily dependent on the DRC market. This disruption poses a severe threat to jobs and livelihoods in the Zambian manufacturing sector, with ripple effects felt throughout the economy.”

a5962.speaker: Ashu Sagar, president of the Zambia Association of Manufacturers
a5962.speech: Added that Zambia’s border closures would make trade between the two countries difficult, considering that there was a deteriorating security situation in the border shared by both countries, and highlighted that ordinary people and cross-border traders had been affected by the closure of crossing points.

a6032.speaker: Pedro Muagura, Park Warden of Gorongosa National Park
a6032.speech: "This is another special day in Gorongosa—an important moment in the restoration of the Park" ; "After many years without them, we're delighted to have these majestic big cats prowling in Gorongosa again."

a6032.speaker: Dr. Rui Branco, Director of Conservation, Gorongosa National Park
a6032.speech: "Everyone pulled together to make it happen and it's a truly collaborative effort that involves multiple partners working across international borders succeed" ; "It's such a privilege for the entire team to be part of such historic conservation work."

a6032.speaker: IUCN Red List of Threatened Species
a6032.speech: Leopards are listed as "Vulnerable" on the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species.

a6032.speaker: Panthera, a leading big cat conservation organisation
a6032.speech: Leopards have retreated from 65% of their historic range in Africa, according to Panthera.

a6314.speaker: Chiyembekezo Ndala, Mukuru enterprise sales manager
a6314.speech: Said their role is to ensure that vulnerable people access their cash easily: "We helped overcome key challenges such as beneficiaries lacking national identity cards and limited access to mobile phones in rural areas."

a6314.speaker: Thomas Msusa, Archbishop of the Blantyre Archdiocese of the Catholic Church
a6314.speech: Commended the partners for their timely support: "I am pleased to be part of this exercise. Many people were affected by EI Nino and it is important that we support them. I also call on other well-wishers to join in."

a6314.speaker: Thomas Msusa, Archbishop of the Blantyre Archdiocese of the Catholic Church
a6314.speech: Urged Malawians to develop long-term strategies to reduce dependency on foreign aid, saying despite gaining independence in 1964, the country remains trapped in poverty: "Our donors are tired of supporting us. Church leaders, traditional authorities and government must work together to make Malawi independent from hunger and poverty."

a6316.speaker: US Embassy in South Sudan (statement)
a6316.speech: Has called on the transitional government to act with urgency to respond to the needs of its citizens, by addressing the causes of humanitarian crisis in the country, including through the transparent use of public revenue to support food security ; describes as tragic and unnecessary that South Sudan, which is endowed with plentiful fertile and arable land, faces acute food insecurity with an estimate 9 million people in dire humanitarian need ; "Many of the causes of food insecurity are in the hands of the South Sudanese leaders to address. These include conflict, economic volatility, and corruption."

a6316.speaker: US Embassy in South Sudan
a6316.speech: Announced in September an additional $100 million in food assistance from the American people to deliver 42,000 metric tons of food to approximately 1 million people expected to face acute food insecurity in South Sudan in the coming months.

a6390.speaker: Rwandan Presidency
a6390.speech: Hailed Chapo's visit — the first to Rwanda since he was elected president in October 2024 — saying it “reaffirmed the shared commitment to further strengthen the existing fruitful bilateral collaboration for the benefit of the people of Rwanda and Mozambique.” ; posted: “This afternoon at Kigali International Airport, President Kagame bid farewell to President Daniel Francisco Chapo at the conclusion of his two-day working visit to Rwanda. The visit reaffirmed the shared commitment to further strengthen the existing fruitful…”

a6390.speaker: President Paul Kagame of Rwanda and President Daniel Chapo of Mozambique
a6390.speech: The two Presidents reaffirmed their commitment to bilateral cooperation in various areas, including peace and security as well as in trade and economic development.

a6390.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique (post on X, August 28, 2025)
a6390.speech: “We have concluded our working visit to the Republic of Rwanda, marked by productive meetings and by the strengthening of the bonds of friendship and cooperation between our countries. Among the main gains, the Status of Forces Agreement (SOFA) and the Memorandum of… stand out.”

a6569.speaker: Algerian Foreign Ministry
a6569.speech: Stated that the two senior diplomats exchanged views on the initiative, which seeks to end hostilities in Gaza, increase humanitarian aid, and prepare for the territory's reconstruction ; added that the two sides also discussed the conditions under which the United Nations Security Council could address the initiative.

a6569.speaker: Ahmed Attaf, Algerian Foreign Minister
a6569.speech: Emphasized the need to seize the opportunities offered by this initiative to ensure a lasting ceasefire in Gaza and move towards a "final, just and lasting resolution" of the Palestinian issue.

a6569.speaker: Antony Blinken, U.S. Secretary of State
a6569.speech: Underscored that the proposal would allow a surge in humanitarian assistance, enable the return of displaced persons to areas throughout Gaza, and permit international reconstruction efforts to begin.

a6569.speaker: Joe Biden, U.S. President
a6569.speech: Announced a three-phase ceasefire proposal in late May, saying it was proposed by the Israeli side and has received positive response from mediators like Egypt and Qatar.

a6809.speaker: Analysts
a6809.speech: say the recent suspension of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) is a wakeup call for African governments – including Lesotho’s – to take responsibility for the health of their citizens ; analysts have urged Prime Minister Sam Matekane to swiftly implement programs to mitigate the impact of the demise of USAID.

a6809.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6809.speech: had ordered the suspension of all foreign aid programmes run by USAID pending a review to assess whether they serve America’s national interests.

a6809.speaker: Elon Musk, one of Trump’s key allies
Trump administration
a6809.speech: had already signalled it will expel USAID’s 10 000 employees and retain it as a mere desk in the State Department with a mere 300 employees at most.

a6809.speaker: A federal judge (US)
a6809.speech: has temporarily halted Mr Trump’s actions.

a6809.speaker: Professor Motlamelle Kapa, National University of Lesotho (NUL)
a6809.speech: said the USAID suspension inevitably holds “severe consequences” for both the government and Basotho who depend on aid. Prof Kapa explained that employees of US-funded projects and non-governmental organizations (NGOs) would lose their livelihoods, further exacerbating Lesotho’s already high unemployment rate. “These job losses will prevent these former employees from contributing to the country’s economic growth and supporting their families,” said Professor Kapa. “Poverty and food insecurity will reach critical levels due to the lost jobs.”

a6809.speaker: Professor Motlamelle Kapa, National University of Lesotho (NUL)
a6809.speech: noted that the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) compact had also been suspended, jeopardizing the anticipated job creation and economic growth. “The project was intended to address food insecurity and high unemployment, but without it, the country will be back to square one,” he added.

a6809.speaker: Professor Motlamelle Kapa, National University of Lesotho (NUL)
a6809.speech: expressed concerns about the uncertainty created by the USAID suspension, emphasizing the need for Lesotho to quickly develop programs to minimize the impact if the withdrawal becomes permanent. He stressed that this was a wake-up call for the country to strive for self-reliance. “We need to build our capacity. Leaders of this country should be ready to build the country’s capacity so that it is able to provide for its people and not be reliant on other countries; otherwise, we will be in a very difficult situation.”

a6809.speaker: Dr Molotsi Monyamane, former Minister of Health (Lesotho)
a6809.speech: said the withdrawal of U.S. funding would impact HIV/AIDS and TB services. However, he quickly emphasized that the government could address these challenges. Dr Monyamane pointed out that the government already bore primary responsibility for HIV treatment, funding antiretroviral (ARV) purchases for 240,152 Basotho. He said: “The government will continue to support related programs, even without U.S. assistance.” He recalled a time before U.S. sponsorship when each ministry allocated 2% of its annual budget to ARV procurement and other HIV-related services, and suggested a return to this practice to reduce reliance on donors. The government currently funds 83% of ARVs, with the Global Fund covering the remaining 17%, Dr Monyamane stated. While acknowledging the U.S. withdrawal would be disruptive, he asserted it would not cripple the healthcare system, and services would continue uninterrupted.

a6809.speaker: Dr Molotsi Monyamane, former Minister of Health (Lesotho)
a6809.speech: stressed the importance of “Lesotho achieving financial independence and establishing a health insurance system”. “That would meet citizens’ health needs and free the government from dependence on external aid,” Dr Monyamane said.

a6809.speaker: Dr Tlohang Letsie, NUL Faculty of Social Sciences
a6809.speech: said the withdrawal of USAID funding will undoubtedly pose significant challenges for Lesotho, because Lesotho had become heavily reliant on American assistance, to the point that even in sectors where Lesotho had the capacity for independent operation, progress remained slow, “with genuine commitment only evident in donor-funded projects requiring financial accountability”. Dr Letsie explained that the loss of US aid would force the government to reallocate funds from other budgeted areas to compensate for the gaps created by the withdrawal.

a6809.speaker: Dr Tlohang Letsie, NUL Faculty of Social Sciences
a6809.speech: offered a more optimistic perspective, suggesting this situation could serve as a “wake-up call” for the nation to prioritize self-reliance. While acknowledging the potential for short-term hardship and disruption, Dr Letsie expressed confidence that Lesotho could eventually achieve greater independence. “It might be hard and painful now, but we will eventually reach the self-reliance stage the country so much needs,” he said.

a6809.speaker: An affected employee of PSI, a PEPFAR-funded organization (name withheld)
a6809.speech: told the Lesotho Times that his contract was suspended on January 27th, following a directive issued on January 24th, and would remain suspended until March 31st. He said they were informed about this suspension via email, and that if there was no new directive to reinstate USAID funding by March 31st, they faced permanent termination of their employment. The PSI employee expressed significant financial and psychological distress due to the suspension. He said as the sole provider for his family, “I am experiencing the mental strain of being unable to afford basic necessities”. He said with his salary, he provided medication for his sick mother, a responsibility he had only managed to start fulfilling when he got his job after many years of unemployment, and he feared the consequences should his contract be permanently terminated. “My reduced income also affects small businesses he supported, such as taxi drivers and street vendors. My inability to contribute to the economy represents a loss for the country. I hope for a resolution that allows employees to return to work,” he said.

a6809.speaker: Selibe Mochoboroane, Minister of Health (Lesotho)
a6809.speech: has assured the 240,152 Basotho on ARV treatment that they would maintain access to their medication despite the USAID freeze. According to Mr Mochoboroane, while USAID funding was crucial for HIV programs in Lesotho, the government already covered 83 percent of the costs for procuring ARVs, with the remaining 17 percent coming from the Global Fund. “This means that although Lesotho’s budget will be strained by the loss of USAID support, the country can still largely provide for its own HIV medication needs,” he said.

a6809.speaker: Selibe Mochoboroane, Minister of Health (Lesotho)
a6809.speech: was concerned about the loss of support staff employed by the various affected NGOs who were involved in the anti-HIV/Aids crusade. He said the ministry had been dependent on various partners, including Jhpiego, the International Centre for AIDS Care and Treatment Programs (ICAP), and the U.S. President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR). “The current structure of the Ministry of Health does not include positions for counsellors,” he stressed, emphasizing the urgent need to address this challenge, as people required counselling prior to being tested for HIV.

a6809.speaker: Selibe Mochoboroane, Minister of Health (Lesotho)
a6809.speech: expressed concern over the potential loss of jobs in the country and the adverse effects that a withdrawal of USAID could have on the recently launched Sustaining Epidemic Control through Unified Prevention (SECURE) project. “Approximately 1,500 health service providers are likely to lose their jobs because of the USAID freeze (if it does become permanent), and my ministry needs 27 million Maloti (M27 million) to pay the salaries of those workers,” Mr Mochoboroane said.

a6879.speaker: Jimmy Donaldson (MrBeast), American YouTuber
a6879.speech: says that he prefers making YouTube videos that make it possible to help people over buying luxurious huge villas and swapping ten cars costing millions of dollars ; says he wants to continue with this kind of charity all his life.

a6879.speaker: Forbes (recent report)
a6879.speech: indicated that the size of his wealth has reached one billion dollars.

a6900.speaker: Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS)
a6900.speech: “Somali Journalists Syndicate (SJS) wishes all Somali journalists a Happy International Workers' Day.”

a6900.speaker: Committee to Protect Journalists
a6900.speech: Somali authorities should immediately release radio journalist Mohamed Abdiwahab Nuur and allow him to work freely, the Committee to Protect Journalists said today.

a6900.speaker: Somalia Health and Demographic Survey (SHDS) Report 2020
a6900.speech: A new report launched today by Somalia—titled the Somalia Health and Demographic Survey (SHDS) Report 2020—offers the country's decision makers and stakeholders vital information on the health and lives of Somali women of childbearing ages and children.

a6900.speaker: Amnesty International
a6900.speech: Addis Ababa municipal authorities have demolished dozens of homes belonging to day labourers over the past three weeks, rendering at least 1,000 people homeless amid the COVID-19 pandemic, Amnesty International said today.

a6900.speaker: US Africa Command (AFRICOM) first quarterly assessment of civilian casualties
a6900.speech: Acknowledges that two Somali civilians were killed and three injured in an air strike.

a6900.speaker: Seif Magango, Amnesty International's Deputy Director
a6900.speech: Reacting to the publication of US Africa Command's (AFRICOM) first quarterly assessment of civilian casualties resulting from its operations in Africa [statement truncated in the article].

a6900.speaker: U.S. Africa Command
a6900.speech: As part of the command's commitment to transparency, U.S. Africa Command is implementing a quarterly report on the status of ongoing and completed civilian casualty allegations and assessments.

a6900.speaker: Open letter to H.E. Mr. Mohamed Abdullahi 'Farmaajo', President of the Federal Republic of Somalia (22 April 2020)
a6900.speech: “Re: Protecting Free Speech and Journalism and Ending Violence Against Journalists. Your Excellency:…”

a7034.speaker: Hakainde Hichilema, President of Zambia (represented by acting Defence Minister Douglas Syakalima)
a7034.speech: Called on Air Forces on the African continent to help one another in humanitarian assistance, disaster relief and search and rescue, saying that by doing so African Air Forces will be honouring the legacy of the forefathers of Africa who believed in a united continent.

a7093.speaker: Detoh Rie, 51-year-old displaced man from Leer county, South Sudan
a7093.speech: "The soldiers attacked our villages and burnt many of our houses. They took our cows and goats and they killed people," he told AFP by telephone from Leer county ; He says he doesn't know if the rest of his family made it out alive as the attackers reduced his village Waay to smouldering ruins.

a7093.speaker: Salva Kiir, President of South Sudan, and Riek Machar, Vice President
a7093.speech: Announced an end to the latest hostilities earlier this month and vowed to make swift progress on implementing key provisions of the 2018 pact.

a7093.speaker: Stephen Taker, commissioner of Leer county
a7093.speech: According to him, the authorities registered 13 930 displaced people on Monday, with many reluctant to head home despite calm reportedly returning to the area. "Everything that they had was all looted," he told AFP, describing the situation as "completely bad".

a7093.speaker: Officials (unnamed)
a7093.speech: Say the number of those displaced could be much higher, with many either unable to access help or too afraid to leave the marshes where they have sought refuge.

a7093.speaker: Kou Tek, 39-year-old displaced father-of-three sheltering in Leer's swamplands
a7093.speech: Described horrific abuses by the armed men who laid waste to his village, telling AFP that women and girls were raped; the attackers also shot dead villagers, he said, adding that he personally saw eight corpses ; Said many displaced people were struggling to survive, with no food or clean water: "Children are taking water from the rivers which are not safe. So a lot of children are having diarrhea and they are not getting any medication," and many children and elderly people "are also dying because of hunger".

a7093.speaker: United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) (statement)
a7093.speech: Has sounded the alarm, warning of "a dire humanitarian situation" in Leer county: "Things got worse over the past weekend with numerous villages south of Leer town being looted and burnt. Critically, Adok port, the second-largest economic hub in (Unity) state, is reported to be destroyed" ; Said Unity is already grappling with the aftermath of the worst flooding to hit the state in 60 years, adding that the "latest upsurge in conflict has exacerbated an already large humanitarian need".

a7093.speaker: Linda Tom, UNMISS spokesperson
a7093.speech: Told AFP that UN peacekeepers "have stepped up patrols and are working closely with communities in Leer... to ease tensions following a surge of violence, including disturbing reports of sexual violence, looting and destruction of property".

a7093.speaker: Paulino Kuch Mawich, coordinator of the UNMISS relief and rehabilitation commission
a7093.speech: Said survivors in Muon, where displaced households have sought shelter in a military training centre, "are in a state of shock": "They need food, shelter, water, and medical care but it is hard to estimate when much-needed humanitarian assistance will reach them."

a7093.speaker: United Nations
a7093.speech: Warned earlier this year that the country risks a return to conflict.

a7134.speaker: Deo Guide Rurema, Minister of Environment, Agriculture and Livestock of Burundi
a7134.speech: "In the communal agriculture and livestock centre, training of trainers will be held, as well as training of community leaders who will popularise and scale up the knowledge acquired in their areas of residence or activity. Agricultural engineers and veterinarians will be available to help the population." ; These centres, he continues, will serve as depots for plant protection products, veterinary products and agricultural inputs.

a7134.speaker: Deo Guide Rurema, Minister of Environment, Agriculture and Livestock of Burundi
a7134.speech: Specified that these centres will address the challenges in the agriculture and livestock sectors: "The population had difficulty finding agricultural monitors, zone assistants or the communal agronomist. When their crops or livestock faced diseases, they did not know where to turn." ; He confides that such centres will be built in all the communes of the country: "This is an innovation in Burundi and it will serve as a model in Africa. We want to be the pilot country in this vision."

a7134.speaker: Deo Guide Rurema, Minister of Environment, Agriculture and Livestock of Burundi
a7134.speech: According to him, the agricultural outreach centre consists of consolidating and pooling different farmers' plots into a single field site: "This facilitates the supervision of farmers and the easy supply of inputs."

a7134.speaker: Deo Guide Rurema, Minister of Environment, Agriculture and Livestock of Burundi
a7134.speech: "Another concept of the government is the development of breeding centres to raise and multiply different animal species, especially cattle, pigs and poultry." ; Said these centres will always be stocked with livestock and will also serve to distribute animals to the population grouped within hill cooperatives, and that they will solve the challenge linked to the adaptation of animals imported from abroad, aiming at the integral and integrated development of the livestock sector ; "The government has set up value chains for the distribution of cattle, pigs and poultry. We are putting in place infrastructure, cowsheds for cows, chicken houses and pigsties," and he invited investors to join this value chain dynamic ; According to him, with the breeding centres it will be possible to collect the animals distributed within the cooperatives in order to process them so as to preserve meat for local consumption and for export.

a7134.speaker: Deo Guide Rurema, Minister of Environment, Agriculture and Livestock of Burundi
a7134.speech: Promised technical and financial support to young people to restock these centres: "The sources of financing are varied for investing in the rural world and improving the income of the population, particularly young people and women."

a7134.speaker: Dina Manirampa, member of the Vaso cooperative on Kiremera hill
a7134.speech: "We are happy to have a communal agriculture and livestock centre. We had difficulty finding agronomists and veterinarians, fertilisers and medicines for animals, but everything will be available here." ; She is delighted that the population will be able to learn techniques there for practising modern agriculture and livestock farming.

a7134.speaker: Sara Mbago Bhunu, Regional Director of the East and Southern Africa Division of IFAD (FIDA)
a7134.speech: For her, the construction of the communal agriculture and livestock centres constitutes great progress for Burundi: "It is very interesting to find women and farmers in the middle of building their own centre." ; According to her, these centres will help rural cooperatives, young people and women to learn modern agriculture and will link them with local and regional markets to sell their harvests.

a7134.speaker: Sara Mbago Bhunu, Regional Director of the East and Southern Africa Division of IFAD (FIDA)
a7134.speech: Said that models and mechanisms involving the rural population in these centres must be put in place, and that the breeding centres serve as a model to be reframed and deepened and to be included in the new PRODER project.

a7134.speaker: Sara Mbago Bhunu, Regional Director of the East and Southern Africa Division of IFAD (FIDA)
a7134.speech: "It would be interesting for Burundian cheese to be found in other countries, notably in Tanzania and the DRC." ; Welcomed the fact that Burundi has managed to introduce the consumption of good-quality milk among the rural population thanks to the milk collection centres and mini-dairies installed by projects financed by IFAD: "In the second phase of the value chain development programme (PRODEFI), small centres for milk processing were installed. Afterwards, we created a synergy with the World Food Programme (WFP) to buy the milk collected at the level of the cooperatives and serve it in school canteens." ; For her, the coordinators will produce documentation so that other countries can learn from Burundi how to develop the dairy sector as well as the value chains for milk production.

a7134.speaker: Sara Mbago Bhunu, Regional Director of the East and Southern Africa Division of IFAD (FIDA)
a7134.speech: Positively appreciates the agro-pastoral activities carried out in the Bitare agro-pastoral complex and calls on young people to go into agribusiness; for her there are many opportunities in rural investment: "We encourage small agricultural producers to seize the opportunities present on the market." ; She also appreciates the practice adopted by the Burundian population of pooling land, which explains the increase in production.

a7134.speaker: Diego King Rekamanyama, owner of the pilot poultry unit in Kinyami, Ngozi commune
a7134.speech: Complains that he faces a lack of market outlets for his eggs and of supply of chicken feed.

a7134.speaker: A manager of the private agro-pastoral centre on Bitare hill
a7134.speech: "Each [cow] can produce at least 12 litres of milk, but that depends on the food consumed." ; He deplores a problem linked to the feeding of this livestock, especially concentrates: "Even our grass plantations are not sufficient to feed these cows every day. Sometimes we need to get supplies elsewhere, but we do not have enough money."

a7134.speaker: Head of an association operating in the Nyakijima II marsh
a7134.speech: "We harvest at least 6 tonnes per hectare. We are continuing research to manage to harvest 8 tonnes on the same area." ; According to him, the population agreed to pool their land and grow rice and beans, which is very productive.

a7134.speaker: David Nzisabira, coordinator of IFAD projects in the northern region
a7134.speech: Said that the population was given a rice variety that can shorten the production cycle, the objective being to harvest more than twice a year: "With PRODEFI, an intensive rice cultivation system (SRI) was introduced. With this system, we went from 1.5 tonnes to more than 5 tonnes per hectare," he declares, appreciating the work of the young people of this locality who help in the maintenance of the irrigation canals.

a7144.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a7144.speech: Has said he will cut all future funding to South Africa over allegations that it is confiscating land and "treating certain classes of people very badly" ; wrote on his social media platform Truth Social on Sunday: "I will be cutting off all future funding to South Africa until a full investigation of this situation has been completed!" ; later said, in a briefing with journalists, that South Africa's "leadership is doing some terrible things, horrible things": "So that's under investigation right now. We'll make a determination, and until such time as we find out what South Africa is doing - they're taking away land and confiscating land, and actually they're doing things that are perhaps far worse than that."

a7144.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, South African President
a7144.speech: "South Africa is a constitutional democracy that is deeply rooted in the rule of law, justice and equality. The South African government has not confiscated any land," Ramaphosa responded in a statement on X on Monday morning ; said that the only funding South Africa received from the US was through the health initiative Pepfar, which represented "17% of South Africa's HIV/Aids programme" ; stressed the government had not confiscated any land, and said the new law was not a "confiscation instrument, but a constitutionally mandated legal process that ensures public access to land in an equitable and just manner as guided by the constitution".

a7144.speaker: Elon Musk, Trump adviser
a7144.speech: "Why do you have openly racist ownership laws?" Mr Musk said to Ramaphosa in a post on X.

a7144.speaker: US government data
a7144.speech: The US allocated about $440m (£358m) in assistance to South Africa in 2023, according to US government data.

a7144.speaker: Donald Trump, then US President (first term)
a7144.speech: Asked the-then US Secretary of State Mike Pompeo to study the country's "farm seizures and expropriations and the large-scale killing of farmers".

a7144.speaker: South African government spokesperson (at the time of Trump's first term)
a7144.speech: South Africa accused Trump of seeking to sow division, with a spokesperson saying he was "misinformed".

a7159.speaker: Han Moon-Hee, President of Korea Railroad Corporation (KORAIL)
a7159.speech: Emphasized the strong historical ties between Ethiopia and Korea, reaffirming Korea’s commitment to supporting Ethiopia’s railway ambitions.

a7159.speaker: Hilina Belachew, CEO of Ethiopian Railway
a7159.speech: Said the MOU marks a new era of collaboration between the two railways, an era built on mutual trust, shared expertise, and a common vision for the advancement of the railway sector.

a7159.speaker: Memorandum of Understanding between ERC and KORAIL (document)
a7159.speech: According to the MOU, the collaboration is expected to improve railway connectivity, enhance logistic efficiency, and promote sustainable economic growth, positioning Ethiopia as a regional hub for modern rail transport.

a7159.speaker: Sileshi Kassa, deputy CEO of Ethiopian Railway and Head of the Railway Infrastructure Development Division
a7159.speech: Noted that a key aspect of the agreement is capacity building, particularly in the areas of studying and operating both existing and new railway lines; previously Ethiopia relied solely on the government to manage railway operations, but this agreement seeks to address that challenge by leveraging international expertise.

a7212.speaker: UN Development Programme (UNDP)
a7212.speech: The agency has said that over 2,000 individuals have earned job opportunities and improved their livelihoods through a cash-for-work initiative of the UNDP funded by Japan in Upper Nile State ; “Through Cash-For-Work and rehabilitation of economic infrastructure, we have created job opportunities and improved livelihoods for over 2,000 individuals from 200+ households,” it said in a statement on Facebook ; UNDP underlined eight key rehabilitated projects in Malakal, which have now been completed ; According to UNDP, these projects are positively impacting vulnerable groups in Malakal.

a7212.speaker: UN Development Programme (UNDP)
a7212.speech: UNDP said it has established a center at the Relief and Rehabilitation Commission’s offices in Juba, aimed at enhancing disaster preparedness, resilience building, and response management.

a7221.speaker: Hassan Ayariga, Founder and Leader of the All People’s Congress (APC)
a7221.speech: Has lauded the economic stewardship of President John Dramani Mahama and the National Democratic Congress (NDC), describing their leadership as a model of fiscal discipline and sound policy-making ; According to Dr Ayariga, the Mahama-led administration’s prudent economic management has led to the stabilization of the Ghanaian Cedi, a development he says has brought relief to various sectors of the economy, particularly importers, traders, entrepreneurs, and consumers.

a7221.speaker: Hassan Ayariga, Founder and Leader of the All People’s Congress (APC)
a7221.speech: In a statement issued by the APC leader, Dr Ayariga called on Ghanaian retailers and wholesalers to reflect the recent economic gains in their pricing strategies. He emphasized that it is both “fair and necessary” for the benefits of a stronger Cedi to be translated into reduced prices of goods and services in the local markets. “This is not only an act of patriotism but a demonstration of solidarity with the Ghanaian people who have endured economic hardships,” he stated. “Lower prices will improve the standard of living, drive consumer demand, and further stimulate economic growth.” ; further appealed to the business community to partner with government efforts in building an economy that is “strong, inclusive, and equitable.”

a7325.speaker: Soliana Shimelis, communications advisor for the National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE)
a7325.speech: According to Soliana Shimelis, the Board is currently implementing pre-electoral operational plans for the upcoming national election, and NEBE has close to a four-billion-Br budget for the current fiscal year ; "We're drawing out our communication strategy," Soliana told Fortune.

a7325.speaker: Soliana Shimelis, communications advisor for the National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE)
a7325.speech: According to Soliana, the bid for the procurement of ballot boxes, ink and biometric voter registration machines has not been announced yet ; "We're still working on our operational plan," she said.

a7325.speaker: Soliana Shimelis, communications advisor for the National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE)
a7325.speech: "The used ballot boxes are still in Hawassa," said Soliana.

a7325.speaker: SEEDS project
a7325.speech: About 50 million people would participate in the upcoming election, according to the SEEDS project.

a7325.speaker: Sources from the National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (anonymous)
a7325.speech: According to sources from the Board, for the Sidama referendum procurements the board floated a closed bid on October 11, 2019, due to time limitations.

a7325.speaker: National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE)
a7325.speech: The Board announced that 98pc of voters in the Sidama referendum cast in favour of the referendum.

a7325.speaker: National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE)
a7325.speech: During the last election in 2015, the Board estimated that 230,000 staff were required to cover 46,000 stations.

a7325.speaker: Dereje Zeleke (PhD), assistant professor of Addis Abeba University's School of Law
a7325.speech: Says that the Board seems to be progressing well in its preparation; according to him the political actors need to show a credible stance and movements for the upcoming election; and recommends that, drawing from past experiences, the feasibility of the election happening peacefully should be looked at and the pressing issues of the peace of the country should be assessed.

a7331.speaker: John Mangudya, Zimbabwe Reserve Bank governor
a7331.speech: Announced that his bank would issue special "bond notes" valued at one-to-one with the US dollar in a bid to ease the cash crisis. He insisted that this was not a new currency. ; Said the bond notes are intended to incentivise exports – and will only be distributed to exporters, in the form of a grant based on the size of the export, to encourage local producers to make products which can be sold abroad, thereby bringing real US dollars into the country.

a7331.speaker: John Mangudya, Zimbabwe Reserve Bank governor
a7331.speech: Maintains that his critics are wrong – and have misunderstood his policy: "We have no hidden agenda."

a7331.speaker: Russell Lamberti, economist, co-author of "When Money Destroys Nations"
a7331.speech: "It does look like they're trying to introduce a new Zim dollar through the back door," said in an interview with the Daily Maverick ; "It doesn't seem very different to me from creating money from thin air, or just printing money. It just seems to be that this is a desperation play, but it hasn't been thought through from a monetary perspective and is dead in the water." ; Says there's almost no chance of the new bond notes holding their value, because they are not backed by anything real; traders won't be able to use them to pay for imports, nor exchange them for US dollars at the reserve bank – because the reserve bank doesn't have any US dollars left – so traders are unlikely to accept them, or will do so at a hefty premium, possibly beginning the steep inflation cycle all over again.

a7331.speaker: Tendai Biti, former finance minister in Zimbabwe's government of national unity
a7331.speech: Said in a statement: "The return of the Zimbabwean dollar marks the gross admission by this regime that it has failed and failed in absolute terms and that it will drag everyone along in the plunge to the abyss that now awaits this economy." ; "It is a cynical, disrespectful and contemptuous move that has absolutely no logic, sense or justification on any rational ground whatsoever… It is a decision that will see many of the remaining companies reach breaking point and simply shut down. Few are prepared to relive the nightmare of the meltdown period of 2007 and 2008."

a7441.speaker: USAID official web page / data
a7441.speech: The data is contained in one of the few web pages that still contain official USAID information after a decision by the Donald Trump government to dismantle the agency, with 2023 being the most recent fiscal year for which complete information is available: Mozambique received the most USAID funds among CPLP members in 2023, a total of US$664.122 million; USAID disbursed a total of US$72 billion in fiscal year 2023, with more than US$16.6 billion sent to Ukraine; Angola followed Mozambique with US$71.320 million, then Brazil with US$68.985 million, Timor-Leste with US$43.688 million, Cape Verde with US$2.961 million, Guinea-Bissau with US$2.910 million, Equatorial Guinea with US$658,700, Sao Tome and Principe with US$216,379 and Portugal with US$6,482.

a7441.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a7441.speech: Accused USAID of being "completely unresponsive," criticizing the agency's "insubordination."

a7441.speaker: Donald Trump, US President, Elon Musk, head of the Office of Government Efficiency (DOGE), and some Republican congressmen
a7441.speech: Have criticized USAID - which oversees humanitarian, development and security programs in about 120 countries - in increasingly harsh terms, accusing it of promoting progressive causes.

a7441.speaker: Experts (anonymous)
a7441.speech: Have assessed that the effects on HIV programs are not yet clear, but the consequences could be rapid and even dangerous.

a7441.speaker: Maria Benvinda Levi, Mozambican Prime Minister
a7441.speech: Admitted last week that the health sector would be the most affected by the suspension of funding. "It is a major challenge because the support from the United States is extremely important, particularly in social areas. So, we will have to see, with our resources, how we can redirect some resources to these areas, so that they are not left without any structure to develop their activities," ; "The main [US] support is for the health area, but there are other sectors that receive less significant support," she acknowledged.
